newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks plunge to new 8-yr low, foreign sales.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks plunge to new 8-yr low, foreign sales.

text.p: Thai stocks plunged on Friday to a new eight-year low as foreigners concerned about the local finance sector's rising non-performing loans and in need of baht supplies sold heavily, brokers said.
The SET index closed down 17.43 points at 530.62 on moderate trade of 5.2 billion baht. The SET-50 index dipped 1.79 points to 37.76.
The central bank has cut off baht supply to foreign speculators after the speculative attack last month.
Thai Farmers Bank slid 4.50 baht to 93, Bangkok Bank dropped six to 142, and Siam Commercial Bank fell nine to 102.
"There seemed to be a major concern about non-performing loans of financial institutions," said one dealer at a local broker. "This triggered heavy selling in finance and bank stocks."
Brokers said foreigners facing severe shortage of baht also dumped stocks in order to raise their much-need funds.

The baht traded at its 13-year high against the dollar in offshore markets as foreign players scrambled to raise funds to cover their short baht positions after mid-May's speculative attack on the currency. -- Anuchit Nguyen (662) 652-0642
